page: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1920s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes a 32 MB L3 cache. It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a local 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, scoring 3138.07 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. However, multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 25024.21 and a PassMark CPU score of 18021.94. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 117.28 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 69.27 GB/sec for large-block write operations. For database workloads, the server handles 15.09 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a PassMark database operations score of 3656.13, both representing average performance tiers.

The server exhibits a clear performance tradeoff between single-core execution and multi-threaded scaling. While single-threaded tasks benefit from top-tier execution speeds, multi-threaded tasks and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. For instance, LLM inference prompt processing using a medium 7B model drops to a weak tier at 18.32 tokens/sec, though text generation for the same model remains average at 12.14 tokens/sec. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the 1920 GB local NVMe SSD, this configuration is suitable for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, static web serving, and moderate data processing tasks that do not require heavy multi-threaded parallelization.
